criteria.text: Prophylaxis to prevent HAE attacks due to C1-esterase inhibitor deficiency (HAE-C1-INH) type 1 or 2.
Patient is 12 years of age or older (FDA labeled age).
Prescribed by or in consultation with an allergist or immunologist.
Andembry will not be used in combination with another agent indicated for HAE prophylaxis (also denial criterion 2).
Patient has a documented history of 3 or more moderate to severe HAE attacks per month.
Medications with an established link to angioedema (e.g. ACE inhibitors, estrogen replacement therapy) have been evaluated and discontinued where appropriate.

Patient has tried and failed or has a documented clinical contraindication to at least one preferred agent approved for HAE prophylaxis from the C1 Esterase Inhibitor or Plasma kallikrein inhibitor classes.

notes: Partial encoding from AK Andembry (garadacimab-gxii), an activated Factor XII (FXIIa) inhibitor monoclonal antibody, Criteria Version 1: Original 08/18/2025; Accepted 9/19/2025; Effective 11/1/2025.

The closed indication covers both diagnosis of HAE-C1-INH type 1 or 2 and use for HAE prophylaxis; no duplicate diagnosis or prophylaxis-only attestation is required. The combination exclusion covers approval and denial criterion 2. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria.
Duration notes only: initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization approval up to 1 year.
Quantity and dosing notes only: loading dose 400mg (two 200mg autoinjectors/syringes) on day 1, followed by 200mg (one autoinjector/syringe) once monthly.
Cautions (notes only): safety in pregnancy or breastfeeding has not been determined. The most common adverse reactions include nasopharyngitis and abdominal pain.
Documentation, duration, dosing, quantity enforcement and cautions require manual review; this pack remains partial.

PDL context: data/alaska/parsed/pdl_index.json and pdl_20260601_text.txt list ANDEMBRY AUTOINJECTOR (SUB-Q) as non-preferred (OFF) in HAE TREATMENTS, effective 6/1/2026. The criteria effective_date remains 2025-11-01.
No evaluate-linked alternatives: Ekterly is for acute attacks, not prophylaxis; Berinert, Cinryze and Takhzyro remain text_only.
